### Arguments

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_pcs`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of principal components to use for the tSNE computation.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `50`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--perplexity`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The perplexity is related to the number of nearest neighbors that is used in other manifold learning algorithms. Larger datasets usually require a larger perplexity. Consider selecting a value between 5 and 50. Different values can result in significantly different results.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `30.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--min_dist`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The effective minimum distance between embedded points. Smaller values will result in a more clustered/clumped embedding where nearby points on the manifold are drawn closer together, while larger values will result on a more even dispersal of points. The value should be set relative to the spread value, which determines the scale at which embedded points will be spread out.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.5`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--metric`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Distance metric to calculate neighbors on.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"euclidean"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--early_exaggeration`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Controls how tight natural clusters in the original space are in the embedded space and how much space will be between them. For larger values, the space between natural clusters will be larger in the embedded space. Again, the choice of this parameter is not very critical. If the cost function increases during initial optimization, the early exaggeration factor or the learning rate might be too high.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `12.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--learning_rate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The learning rate for t-SNE optimization. Typical values range between 10.0 and 1000.0.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1000.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--random_state`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The random seed to use for the tSNE computation.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/dimred/tsne/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/dimred/tsne);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/dimred/tsne/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
